## Advice

**1. Buy the thermometer.** This is the one concrete stumbling block your memories actually record — you asked on May 30 whether 2-3 hours of waiting was enough without checking temperature. For yogurt it isn't: you need 180–185°F to scald, then a real drop to 110–120°F before the culture goes in. Too hot kills the culture, too cool lets the wrong bacteria win, and "about 2 hours" varies by cooker and kitchen temperature. An instant-read thermometer removes the single biggest source of inconsistency you have right now.

**2. Learn your specific cooker's temperament.** Slow cookers vary a lot. Fill yours with water, run it on low for 4 hours, and take the temperature — if it's well above ~200°F, yours runs hot and every recipe time you read needs shortening. This is worth doing once and is especially useful to you as a blogger, since it tells you whether your published times will translate to readers' machines.

**3. Cut the liquid, roughly by half.** Nothing evaporates under a sealed lid, and vegetables release their own water. Watery results are the most common complaint from new users, and it will hit your plant-based dishes hardest.

**4. Stop lifting the lid.** Each peek loses steam and adds roughly 20–30 minutes.

**5. Brown first.** Sear the meat and sweat the onions/garlic/spices in a pan before they go in. The slow cooker can't brown anything, so all of that flavor has to be built beforehand. Your beef stew already worked — this is what takes it from good to show-stopper.

**6. Season at the end, not the start.** Long cooking mutes salt, acid, and spice. Taste and correct in the last 20 minutes; that's when the splash of lemon or vinegar goes in.

**7. Sequencing for your plant-based cooking:** add acid (tomatoes, vinegar, lemon) *late* if you're cooking dried beans — acid keeps them tough. Add delicate things at the end too: fresh herbs, greens, coconut/plant milk, cooked pasta or grains. Root vegetables go on the bottom, near the heat.

**8. Thickening, gluten-free:** since you're eating GF, skip the flour roux anyway — stir in a cornstarch or arrowroot slurry in the last 30 minutes on high, or blend out a ladle of the beans/vegetables and return it. Also double-check that stocks and sauces are certified GF.

**9. For the cashew yogurt specifically:** the levers are cashew-to-water ratio (less water = thicker), blend time, straining through a nut milk bag, and a full chill. Note that plant bases don't set from culture alone the way dairy does — a starch or agar and a dedicated vegan starter culture do most of the structural work there.

**10. Since you blog:** log time, temperature, and liquid volume on every attempt. Slow cooker results are hard to reproduce blind, and your notes are what will make a recipe reliable for readers.
